Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity — GPU options, TPS & concurrency (follow-up)

Hi Anna & Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — helpful convo. Quick recap and the next asks so we can put together a concrete Dedicated proposal (cost + recommended SKU):

Recap from our call:
- Primary use case: real-time assistant inside your product (search + conversational generation).
- Target SLA: p95 < 400ms for short sessions, acceptable tail to 700ms for long-context calls.
- Current model baseline: Llama-2-70B and evaluation on a smaller gen model for chat.
- Peak traffic expectation (your estimate): ~600 TPS burst for embeddings + gen; steady-state ~140 TPS.

Immediate items we need to size Dedicated accurately:
1) Traffic breakdown: peak vs steady TPS by endpoint (chat / embeddings / rerank).
2) Token mix: average prompt tokens and average generated tokens per chat turn (if approximate, provide ranges).
3) Sequence length distribution: % of requests <128, 128-512, 512-2048, >2048 tokens.
4) Model commitment: which model(s) you plan to serve on Dedicated (Llama-2-70B v1, Mistral, or a quantized variant).
5) KV/prefix cache expectations (do sessions reuse context heavily?).

Attached a blank sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx) — please fill the highlighted cells for TPS and token mix. Also included is a sample MAL POC map we use for internal ops.

Preliminary guidance (so you have directional expectations):
- If you want to serve Llama-2-70B with 1.5k token context and sustain bursts ~600 TPS, H100-class GPUs are the safe recommendation (or partitioned A100 setup with aggressive quantization/caching).
- For steady-state ~140 TPS with average responses <256 tokens, an A100 conf (8x A100-style nodes) could work if you use aggressive KV caching and batching.
- Concurrency: we typically target 50-120 concurrent active requests per GPU depending on model and quantization.

Next steps / asks: please return the sizing sheet and a short note on preferred deployment mode (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private VPC) and whether procurement should be looped now. Once we have the traffic numbers I can run a quick Dedicated SKU simulation and share a cost-backed recommendation.

If easier, we can jump on a 20-min follow-up tomorrow morning — propose 10:00-10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.inference

Hi Alex — thanks for the recap and for the worksheet. Attaching our traffic export and a short note here to speed things along.

Quick answers inline:
1) Traffic breakdown (approx):
   - chat/generation: peak burst 480 TPS, steady 120 TPS
   - embeddings (async): peak 220 TPS, steady 60 TPS (we can move embeddings off Dedicated if cost demands)
   - rerank: negligible (<10 TPS)
2) Token mix (avg):
   - prompt: 110 tokens
   - generation: 320 tokens
3) Sequence distribution (by %):
   - <128: 28%
   - 128-512: 52%
   - 512-2048: 18%
   - >2048: 2% (rare long-context sessions)
4) Models: primary is Llama-2-70B quantized (we're testing q4_0 and q5_0). We may run a distilled Mistral for low-latency fallbacks.
5) Cache: sessions reuse conversation context in ~70% of interactions (high reuse).

I've attached brightfuture-traffic-summary.csv (export) and a short procurement note. Procurement is looped here — procurement will need an initial SOW and sample PO before moving to legal.

We can do the follow-up tomorrow at 10:00 PT — that works for me.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity — GPU options, TPS & concurrency (follow-up)

Anna — hugely helpful, thanks. A few clarifying items so my sizing sim is accurate: 

- For the chat/generation slices, when you say "generation avg 320 tokens", is that inclusive of the prompt tokens or separate (i.e., total tokens per request)? We model cost differently if 320 = prompt+response vs 320 = response only.
- On quantization: which quant backend are you using to test q4_0 / q5_0 (ex: bitsandbytes, custom build)? Any perf numbers you'd seen locally (latency per token on a single A100/H100)?
- For embeddings: are you open to a hybrid strategy (Dedicated for chat + Hosted for embeddings) to lower Dedicated footprint? If embeddings are bursty but non-critical latency, routing to Hosted can save ~20-30% on Dedicated cost.

Directional sizing notes from running the sim with your numbers:
- Assuming 480 TPS burst for chat and 320 average response tokens (prompt + resp = 430 total tokens per request), to keep p95 under 400ms we'd look at H100-class nodes with 12–16 GPUs total (rough estimate) if you want single-model headroom. With aggressive KV caching and batching you can lower GPUs by ~20%.
- If you adopt a hybrid approach (hosted embeddings + dedicated chat), the Dedicated pool drops to ~8–10 H100s for the same p95 target.
- Concurrency target per GPU: 70–110 active requests depending on quantization level and effective batch window.

I'll slot these numbers into the sizing sheet and hand to Lauren and Aditya to produce a quote. Agenda for the 10:00 PT call: I can present two SKU options (single H100 pool vs mixed A100+H100 with quantization savings) and a short cost comparison.

On the call you can expect the following deliverables from us within 48 hours after we get the updated sizing sheet filled:
- Detailed SKU recommendation and cost breakdown
- Suggested rollout plan (canary -> 50% -> 100%) with fallback rules to Hosted API
- A short ops checklist for KV cache priming and checkpointing frequency

Thanks — talk shortly.

—Alex

Also include: expected provisioning lead time, proposed canary rollout (traffic slices), and a short ops playbook bullet list for cache priming. I will own the customer-facing slide + 1-page SOW.
